get.description:
Lists `Bible` objects authorized for the current API Key. This includes Creative Commons and Public Domain Bibles, as well as any Bibles licensed via a **Starter** or **Pro Plan**.

A `Bible` object represents a single translation (NIV, ESV, etc.) of the Bible. Each Bible is accessible via its **Bible ID**, a string
consisting of a 16-digit unique string followed by a _publication number_ (`-01`, `-02`). A few popular examples are:

| Bible                                  | Bible ID              |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| King James Version (**KJV**)           | `de4e12af7f28f599-01` |
| Douay-Rheims (**DRA**)                 | `179568874c45066f-01` |
| Christian Standard Bible (**CSB**)     | `a556c5305ee15c3f-01` |

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: ISO 639-3 three digit language code used to filter results

parameters.name: abbreviation
parameters.description: Bible abbreviation to search for

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Bible name to search for

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma separated list of Bible Ids to return

parameters.name: include-full-details
parameters.description: When `true`, the returned Bibles will include additional Bible details (e.g. copyright and promo info)

get.description:
Gets a `Passage` object for a given `bibleId` and `passageId`.

A `Passage` object represents an arbitrary range of verses from the Bible. These ranges are not predefined values, but instead depend
on the given input, known as a **Passage ID**. A **Passsage ID** consists of two [Verse](https://docs.api.bible/guides/verses) IDs separated by a `-`. These
**Verse IDs** can span chapters and books, though passages are limited to 200 verses.
A few passage examples are:

| Verse Range                             | Passage ID          |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| Genesis 1:1 - Genesis 2:3               | `GEN.1.1-GEN.2.3`   |
| John 3:1 - John 3:16                    | `JHN.3:1-JHN.3.16`  |
| 1 Corinthians 16:1 - 2 Corinthians 1:23 | `1CO.16.1-2CO.1.23` |

In addition to information about the given passage, this endpoint will also return all verse content included in that passage within the `content` field.

get.description:
Lists `Section` objects for a given `bibleId` and `bookId`

A `Section` object represents a known range of verses in the Bible, typically tied to a story. Each Section is accessible via its **Section ID**,
a string consisting of a [Book](https://docs.api.bible/guides/books) ID and a section number. Not every Bible has sections enabled. For Bibles with sections enabled,
sections are sequential and _should_ cover nearly every verse if queried in order.
A few examples from the book of Genesis are:

| Section Title | Verse Range                | Section ID |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | ---------- |
| The Beginning | Genesis 1:1 - Genesis 2:3  | `GEN.S1`   |
| Adam and Eve  | Genesis 2:4 - Genesis 2:25 | `GEN.S2`   |
| The Fall      | Genesis 3:1 - Genesis 3:24 | `GEN.S3`   |

*Note: This endpoint does not return verse content*

get.description:
A search will attempt to match all verses with the list of keywords provided in the query string.
The order of the keywords does not matter, however _all listed keywords must be
present in a verse for it to be considered a match_.

Wildcard searches are supported, and can be used to match partial results:

| Wildcard | Description                    | Example                                                      |
| -------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `*`      | Matches any character sequence | "wo\*d" finds text such as "word", "world", and "worshipped" |
| `?`      | Matches any single character   | "l?ve" finds text such as "live" and "love"                  |

The `text` property of each search result contains only the verse text, it does not
contain footnote references or additional formatting. However, more information on a verse can be queried directly by
[fetching a single verse](https://docs.api.bible/guides/verses#fetching-a-single-verse).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Comma-separated search keywords or a passage reference. Supported wildcards are `*` and `?`. The `*` wildcard matches any character sequence (e.g. searching for "wo*d" finds text such as "word", "world", and "worshipped"). The `?` wildcard matches any matches any single character (e.g. searching for "l?ve" finds text such as "live" and "love").

get.description:
Lists `AudioBible` objects authorized for current API Key.

**Audio Bibles** are nearly identical to [Bibles](https://docs.api.bible/guides/bibles),
including their content structure. Audio Bibles, however, have one audio file for each chapter and therefore cannot be queried at the verse level. This is why
Audio Bibles are queried separately from normal Bibles.

Audio Bible availability via API.Bible requires special licensing. For more information, please reach out to [support@api.bible](mailto:support@api.bible).

get.description:
Gets a single `AudioChapter` object for a given `bible` and `chapterId`.

A presigned link to the mp3 audio file for this audio chapter will be included in the `resourceUrl` field. This link is unique to your request and will
will expire, so it is recommended to download that audio file using that link as quickly as you are able. It is **not** recommended
that you stream audio directly from the provided link, as you will run into a number of ongoing issues.

Some audio chapters will include `timecodes`. These allow you to match verses in a chapter to a specific time code in the audio file.
This can be helpful if you are using both text and audio Bibles and would like to highlight the verse as it is being read.

parameters.name: chapterId
parameters.description: Id of the Chapter to fetch

firstVerseOrgId.description: The `orgId` of the last verse in this section. Typically not relevant

lastVerseOrgId.description: The `orgId` of the last verse in this section, typically not relevant.

Section.title: Section
Section.description:
A **Section** object represents a known range of verses in the Bible, typically tied to a story, including verse content. Not every Bible has sections enabled. For Bibles with sections enabled,
sections are sequential and _should_ cover nearly every verse if queried in order.

id.description:
A string consisting of a [Book](https://docs.api.bible/guides/books) ID and a section number. A few examples from the book of Genesis are:

| Section Title | Verse Range                | Section ID |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | ---------- |
| The Beginning | Genesis 1:1 - Genesis 2:3  | `GEN.S1`   |
| Adam and Eve  | Genesis 2:4 - Genesis 2:25 | `GEN.S2`   |
| The Fall      | Genesis 3:1 - Genesis 3:24 | `GEN.S3`   |

bibleId.description: The **Bible ID** this section is associated with

bookId.description: The **Bible ID** this section is associated with

firstVerseId.description: The `id` of the first verse in this section

lastVerseId.description: The `id` of the last verse in this section

firstVerseOrgId.description: The `orgId` of the last verse in this section. Typically not relevant

lastVerseOrgId.description: The `orgId` of the last verse in this section, typically not relevant.

next.description: Information about the next **Section**, if one exists. Can be used to navigate the Bible one section at a time.

id.description: The next section's `id`

previous.description: Information about the previous **Section**, if one exists. Can be used to navigate the Bible backwards one verse at a time.

id.description: The previous section's `id`

SearchResponse.title: Search Response
SearchResponse.description: The result of executing a search query. Paginated using the `limit` and `offset` query parameters.

total.description: The total number of search results

verses.description: The verses that match the search `query`. If a passage was searched rather than keywords, this array will be empty.

id.description:
A string consisting of a [Book](https://docs.api.bible/guides/books) ID, a chapter number, and a verse number. A few examples are:

| Verse           | Verse ID   |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| Genesis 1:1     | `GEN.1.1`  |
| John 3:16       | `JHN.3.16` |
| Revelation 21.4 | `REV.21.4` |

orgId.description: The ID assigned to this verse by it's publishing organization, typically not relevant.

bibleId.description: The **Bible ID** this verse is associated with

bookId.description: The **Book ID** this verse is associated with

chapterId.description: The **Chapter ID** this verse is associated with

reference.description: The full reference for this verse

text.description: Verse content, formatted as `text`. Additional information about this verse can be fetched by making a request to `/bibles/{bibleId}/verses/{verseId}`

AudioBibleSummary.title: Audio Bible Summary
AudioBibleSummary.description: An **AudioBibleSummary** object is a minimal representation of a single auditory translation (NIV, ESV, etc.) of the Bible, typically attached to an associated **Bible**

id.description:
A string
consisting of a 16-digit unique string followed by a _publication number_ (`-01`, `-02`). A few popular examples are:

| Bible                                  | Bible ID              |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| King James Version (**KJV**)           | `de4e12af7f28f599-01` |
| Douay-Rheims (**DRA**)                 | `179568874c45066f-01` |
| Christian Standard Bible (**CSB**)     | `a556c5305ee15c3f-01` |

name.description: Name of this Audio Bible version

nameLocal.description: Localized name of this Audio Bible version

description.description: Description of this Audio Bible version

descriptionLocal.description: Localized description of this Audio Bible version

AudioBible.title: Audio Bible
AudioBible.description: An **AudioBible** object represents a single auditory translation (NIV, ESV, etc.) of the Bible. For simplicity's sake, this model is identical to a `Bible`.

AudioChapter.title: Audio Chapter
AudioChapter.description: An **Audio Chapter** object represents a single auditory chapter of the Bible. Rather than verses or sections, audio chapter verse content is stored at the chapter level.

id.description:
A string consisting of a [Book](https://docs.api.bible/guides/books) ID and a chapter number. A few examples are:

| Chapter       | Chapter ID |
| ------------- | ---------- |
| Genesis 1     | `GEN.1`    |
| John 3        | `JHN.3`    |
| Revelation 22 | `REV.22`   |

bibleId.description: The **Bible ID** this audio chapter is associated with

bookId.description: The **Book ID** this audio chapter is associated with

resourceUrl.description:
A presigned link to the audio file for this audio chapter. This link
will expire, so it is recommended to download that audio file using that link as quickly as you are able. It is **not** recommended
that you stream audio directly from the provided link, as you will run into a number of ongoing issues.

timecodes.description: Allows you to match verses in a chapter to a specific time code in the audio file. This can be helpful if you are using both text and audio Bibles and would like to highlight a verse as it is being read.

end.description: The timestamp when this verse ends

start.description: The timestamp when this verse starts

verseId.description: The **Verse ID** being read at this timestamp

expiresAt.description: The timestamp the presigned `resourceUrl` link will expire

reference.description: The full reference for this audio chapter

next.description: Information about the next **AudioChapter**, if one exists. Can be used to navigate the Bible one audio chapter at a time.

id.description: The next audio chapter's `id`

previous.description: Information about the previous **AudioChapter**, if one exists. Can be used to navigate the Bible backwards one chapter at a time.

id.description: The previous audio chapter's `id`
ISO 639-3 three digit language code

script.description: The type of script used for this language
